brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Cohesive dark palette with category-coded accent dots that tie sidebar legend to card tags clearly
Confident typographic hierarchy: tracked-out section labels, crisp titles, and quiet metadata reinforce calm canvas feel
Spatial proximity concept is legible — Research, Documentation, and Design clusters read as topical neighborhoods
dominant_weaknesses: Cards overlap and clip text (Sprint Planning covers Project Roadmap, Figma covers Design System), breaking readability not aesthetics
Section labels float ambiguously between clusters; no connective tissue, edges, or zones to make proximity meaningful
No visible affordances for canvas behavior — pan, zoom, drag, or grouping — so the spatial metaphor feels static and decorative
fix_priorities: Resolve overlap collisions: introduce a soft auto-layout or magnetic spacing so cards never occlude each other's content
Add cluster affordances — subtle bounding regions, tinted halos, or connective lines — so topic proximity becomes structural not coincidental
Signal interactivity with hover lifts, drag shadows, and a minimap or zoom indicator to anchor the spatial canvas
Tighten section-label placement so each title clearly owns its cluster rather than drifting in negative space
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective land well via palette and concept, but behavioral usability collapses under overlapping cards and missing canvas controls.
rationale.intent_fit: It gestures convincingly at a spatial document canvas but undermines the brief by letting cards collide and offering no spatial-interaction language.
